mintAuthority.summary: FUSD is a native Zano Confidential Asset (asset id 8614…4f8f), not a smart contract: Zano has no contract VM, so issuance is a consensus-level EMIT operation that only the holder of the asset-owner key 497d6b7a…c7c1 can sign. That single key can emit up to the descriptor's total_max_supply of 1e15 fUSD against 11.4M fUSD outstanding. The ceiling is roughly 87 million times circulation, so the mint is unbounded in practice, and it can hand ownership to any other key. The white paper's over-collateralization and 'DAO' framing is an off-chain operating policy: Zano consensus checks only the owner signature and the max-supply ceiling, never the ZANO reserve. total_max_supply is immutable post-deployment, so no cap-raise path exists.

controls.capDescription: Nominal descriptor ceiling total_max_supply = 10000000000000000000 base units (1e15 fUSD at decimal_point 4) against a current_supply of 114000000000 base units (11,400,000 fUSD). The ceiling is ~87,700,000x circulation and is immutable post-deployment, so it bounds nothing economically: emission is treated as unbounded.

controls.evidence: At Zano height 3770932 (2026-07-14), get_asset_info for asset 86143388bd056a8f0bab669f78f14873fac8e2dd8d57898cdb725a2d5e2e4f8f returned asset_descriptor.owner = 497d6b7acd06401c59b2d52a3967968e8ca507a25f80e44d2bb4b5f8a348c7c1 (non-null: ownership is held, not renounced), owner_eth_pub_key = "" (empty), total_max_supply = 10000000000000000000, current_supply = 114000000000, decimal_point = 4, hidden_supply = false. Two independent daemons (node.zano.org and 37.27.100.59:10500) returned byte-identical descriptors. Per Zano docs the owner key is the sole authority validated for EMIT and UPDATE, and total_max_supply cannot be changed after deployment. Zano exposes no contract VM, so there is no minter registry, role admin, timelock, or proxy layer above this key; it is a single ed25519 public key with no on-chain multisig or threshold structure.

review.reviewer: Codex SOL-V mint-tier research; Sol economic-posture batch 2026-08-15
review.sourceFreeRationale: Resolved directly from Zano consensus state; the prior 'unverifiable privacy chain' disposition was wrong. Zano hides transaction amounts and addresses, but asset descriptors (owner key, supply, cap) are public and readable over the standard daemon RPC.
review.evidence: Historical authority evidence retained: at Zano height 3770932 (2026-07-14), get_asset_info on node.zano.org, corroborated by daemon 37.27.100.59:10500, returned asset 86143388bd056a8f0bab669f78f14873fac8e2dd8d57898cdb725a2d5e2e4f8f with owner 497d6b7acd06401c59b2d52a3967968e8ca507a25f80e44d2bb4b5f8a348c7c1, empty owner_eth_pub_key, total_max_supply 10000000000000000000, current_supply 114000000000 and decimal_point 4. Zano's cited documentation validates EMIT and UPDATE against that owner key and makes the nominal maximum immutable. The white paper's collateralized-ZANO issuance policy does not constrain consensus-level emission; off-chain key custody remains unverified. ORCHESTRATOR-AUTHORIZED adverse-pin correction — owner review required: on 2026-10-20, the current issuer white paper, live metrics, reserve-verification page, FAQ and legal page were re-opened. They publish reserve/supply figures, a coverage ratio and a view-only wallet verification method, but disclose no complete mechanical whole-liability-to-backing reconciliation procedure, committed recurring report series or enforced reserve check at every mint. The August 15 sentence inferring continuous whole-supply reconciliation from a live dashboard and hourly/daily display was unsupported; withdraw reconciliation to unknown, not none. The cited FinCEN MSB search neither establishes prudential supervision nor proves its absence; supervision is unknown. Preserve the August 15 review start, July authority pins, cap semantics and all other adverse facts. This removes unsupported process credit; it does not assert measured non-reconciliation, an active mint incident or insolvency.
